open_obligations: Check that 'a more limited class of problems' corresponds to doubly-efficient debate's need for a polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript (LIM-HUMAN-VERIFIABLE) rather than another restriction
Read p2 L86 to p3 L7 of the citing paper, which elaborates the same cost (debaters must write out the full human-judgeable argument) but spans a page break
Note the shared first author: both papers are by Brown-Cohen et al., so the critique is partly self-assessment
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate paper: doubly-efficient debate (Brown-Cohen et al.) solves a narrower class
in.rationale: Brown-Cohen et al. (2023/2024) give a debate protocol where an efficient honest debater wins but the full human-judgeable argument must be verifiable; the authors name the resulting restriction to a more limited problem class as the cost of that design. It is an argument about the cited protocol's scope, not a new result on it, so CRITIQUES.
in.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Which problem classes debate protocols with efficient honest debaters can handle; holds within complexity-theoretic debate models

text: The authors state that a key requirement and limitation for real-world use is that the debating models must be able to produce (potentially extensive) natural-language reasoning traces for the problem such that (potentially extensive) careful human analysis could have judged the reasoning correct. Given this, they say even very complex computations could be verified by querying human judgements on only a single step.
title: Limitation: needs a (possibly long) human-verifiable natural-language reasoning trace
